deep.reconstruction:
There are no mathematical derivations on this page. It is a short programmatic and philosophical note in two parts, separated by horizontal rules.

(1) Against the 'Ignorabimus'. 'It is a kind of intellectual sadism, in which the public popular speakers so gladly wallow, in proclaiming the Ignorabimus. Let us rather set against this deterrent word the positive, more joyful, science-glad Non ignorabimus. For to us mathematicians at least there is no Not-Being-Able (Nicht-Können).' This answers Emil du Bois-Reymond's 'Ignoramus et ignorabimus' (1872; 'Die sieben Welträthsel', 1880). It is the same theme as Hilbert's Paris problem lecture (1900: 'in der Mathematik gibt es kein Ignorabimus'), the 'Axiomatisches Denken' circle (1917/18) and the Königsberg address 'Naturerkennen und Logik' (1930: 'Wir müssen wissen, wir werden wissen').

(2) A claim about the formal rules of proof theory. 'Our rules: substitutions (Einsetzungen), abbreviations (Abkürzungen, i.e. definitions), attaching arguments also to statements (Argument-anhängen auch an Aussagen) are definitive, complete, and incapable of any extension. For our thinking is absorbed in their operation (Handeln) and is finite (no witchcraft!).'

In modern terms, these are the structural rules of a Hilbert-style formalism:
- uniform substitution for variables, including formula and predicate variables;
- introduction of defined symbols as abbreviations;
- forming propositional functions by attaching argument places to statements (higher-order or predicate variables).

The page asserts that this rule set is closed and complete, and that finitary thought consists exactly in operating with these rules. This is the finitist creed of the Hilbert programme (cf. 'Neubegründung der Mathematik' 1922, 'Über das Unendliche' 1926, 'Die Grundlagen der Mathematik' 1928). The previous page's remarks on the 'Überbewusstsein' of axiomatics and on '=' as the negation of '≠' place the sheet among Hilbert's 1920s or c.1930 philosophical jottings, probably material for a lecture or address.

No implicit steps had to be filled in.
errors: There is no computational error to report. Historically, the strong claim that the formal rules are 'vollständig und keiner Erweiterung fähig', together with the general 'kein Nicht-Können', is the optimism that Gödel's incompleteness theorems (1931) showed untenable for any consistent, effectively axiomatized system containing arithmetic. It holds only if 'complete' means completeness of the rule repertoire, not completeness of the theory. The text does not specify which is meant.

results.what: Programmatic rejection of du Bois-Reymond's Ignorabimus in favour of 'Non ignorabimus'; for mathematicians there is no 'Nicht-Können'
results.modern_name: Hilbert's 'Wir müssen wissen – wir werden wissen' / solvability-of-every-problem axiom

results.what: Claim that the formal rules (substitution, abbreviation/definition, attaching arguments to statements) are definitive, complete and non-extendable, and that finitary thinking is exhausted by operating with them
results.modern_name: Finitist foundation of Hilbert's programme; structural rules of a Hilbert-style calculus (uniform substitution, definitional extension, predicate/propositional-function formation)
results.usually_credited_to: David Hilbert and Paul Bernays (1920s proof theory)

deep.surprise_reason: Both themes are well known as Hilbert's. The anti-Ignorabimus stance is famous from 1900 and 1930, and finitist confidence in the formal rules is the core of the Hilbert programme. The phrasing 'intellektueller Sadismus' and the explicit claim that the rules are 'keiner Erweiterung fähig' are colourful unpublished details, but they are not new content.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'wenn[?] sie das Ignorabimus verkünden' should read 'indem sie das Ignorabimus verkünden'. The manuscript has 'inden/indem', not 'wenn'.

Otherwise the transcription matches the image: 'Sadismus, in dem', 'wissenschaftsfrohe Non ignorabimus', 'giebt es kein Nicht-Können', 'Argument-anhängen auch an Aussagen sind definitiv, vollständig und keiner Erweiterung fähig', 'ist finit (keine Hexerei!)'.
